summary: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data.
takeaways: Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data.
We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video dataset purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling.
Experiments further demonstrate that training on GameVerse substantially extends the temporal horizon of interactive world models.
